title: An API for MoQ: provision your own isolated relays
summary: Cloudflare now lets developers provision their own isolated Media over QUIC relays with separate credentials for publishers and viewers, deployable in seconds across its global network.
details: Isolated relays are carved out of Cloudflare's existing global network rather than requiring dedicated servers, so they deploy in seconds without picking a region or configuring a load balancer.
Separate access tokens for publishers and subscribers mean a viewer's credentials can't be used to hijack the stream, enabling permissioned use cases like live auctions.

The API also adds support for MoQ draft-16, which lets publishers push tracks before subscribers ask for them and lets subscribers request whole namespaces of tracks at once, cutting connection latency.

title: How to build interactive experiences with canvases
summary: GitHub added canvases to the Copilot app, letting an AI agent build a shared, clickable visual workspace, like a card sorter or a diagram, instead of only responding in text.
details: Users start a canvas with a /create-canvas command describing what they want, and the canvas updates live as the agent works while the user clicks, edits, and reacts to it.
Example canvases include a swipeable issue-triage board, an interactive diagram of how a codebase's components relate, and a view of active Git worktrees that can be cleaned up with a button click.
The pattern extends beyond coding tasks: one example canvas searches Slack, Teams, email, and docs to surface who on a team has relevant expertise on a topic.

title: How the 2026 World Cup affected Internet traffic
summary: Cloudflare's traffic data shows the 2026 World Cup reshaped internet usage worldwide, with late-night matches roughly doubling traffic and one quarterfinal moving traffic more than any final.
details: Matches played overnight or early morning caused the biggest traffic shifts, sometimes more than doubling normal traffic, while daytime matches barely moved traffic because people were already online.

The single match that shifted a country's traffic the most wasn't a final or semifinal but Argentina's quarterfinal win over Switzerland, and Argentina's matches overall swung the typical country's traffic by about 17%.

Behavior at halftime and hydration breaks split into two camps: most of the 44 countries studied saw a traffic bump during breaks, but a smaller group, including Algeria and Tunisia, saw traffic dip, likely from heavier streaming.

title: How Searchable ships customer-requested features in 30 minutes on Vercel
summary: Searchable, a startup that tracks how brands appear in AI search answers, used Vercel's AI SDK and AI Gateway to cut the time to ship a customer-requested feature down to about 30 minutes.
details: Routing all model calls through Vercel's AI Gateway let the team swap between AI models to test and compare them without rotating API keys or rewriting code for each provider's SDK.
The company says the setup increased development speed by roughly 2 to 5 times and let them process over 100 billion tokens without adding proportional engineering overhead.
Searchable's product tracks brand visibility across AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude, and recommends changes to improve it.

title: GenRec: Towards LLM-Native Recommendation at Netflix
summary: Netflix built GenRec, a recommendation ranker based on a fine-tuned LLM, which matched or beat its existing production ranker while needing far less labeled training data.
details: GenRec turns user watch history, title metadata, and context into plain text prompts for an LLM, replacing thousands of hand-crafted numeric features with what Netflix calls context engineering.

In production A/B tests across about 10% of Netflix traffic over four weeks, GenRec improved both short-term and long-term engagement metrics while using 10 to 40 times fewer labeled examples than the existing ranker.
Netflix serves GenRec in a prefill-only mode, scoring the whole catalog in a single forward pass instead of generating text token by token, which keeps inference costs manageable at scale.

title: Stacked sessions and pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app
summary: A GitHub engineer used the Copilot app's stacked-sessions feature to chain AI coding sessions into dependent pull requests, modernizing an old codebase without one giant PR.
details: Rather than one large pull request, each new Copilot session can branch off the previous session's unmerged branch, splitting the work into a chain of smaller, reviewable PRs that build on each other.
The workflow let the author ship a pull request for work already done and start a fresh session for the next piece of work without losing the dependency between the two branches.
Stacking sessions helped avoid scope creep while modernizing a decade-old codebase stuck on outdated dependencies like React 15 and Less, by keeping each PR focused on one concern.

title: Dogfooding at scale: migrating cdnjs to Cloudflare’s Developer Platform
summary: Cloudflare finished moving cdnjs, which serves about 9 billion requests a day, fully onto its own Developer Platform, and had to raise several of its own platform limits to make that work.
details: The migration replaced a mix of GCP Functions, a git-sync VM, and Workers with a stack built on R2 for file storage, KV for metadata, Workflows for the ingestion pipeline, and Containers for compression.

Copying millions of existing files without regenerating them was necessary to keep pinned Subresource Integrity hashes valid, and doing so exposed a Workers subrequest limit that Cloudflare then raised from 1,000 to 10 million per invocation on paid plans.

cdnjs still serves roughly 12% of all websites and a large share of the JavaScript CDN market, partly because AI coding assistants frequently reference it, having trained on 15+ years of tutorials that point to it.

title: Shopify and Vercel are rebuilding Hydrogen for faster storefronts
summary: Shopify and Vercel are rebuilding Hydrogen, Shopify's headless storefront framework, to be framework- and runtime-agnostic and to speed up custom feature development for retailers.
details: The rebuilt Hydrogen no longer locks storefronts into one framework; it runs with Next.js, Nuxt, Svelte, or other JavaScript frameworks and ships type-safe API clients and built-in cart state.

One retailer using the new framework reported cutting feature development time from months to about a week, because common e-commerce patterns are now built into the framework instead of hand-rolled each time.
A new Standard Actions feature adds support for agentic commerce, letting AI agents take actions directly on a storefront rather than just browsing it.

title: Why we cannot wait for better post-quantum signature algorithms
summary: NIST is advancing nine new post-quantum signature algorithms as potential candidates for future standardization. We take a closer look at all of them, and argue that while they are in the works and show great potential, we should use ML-DSA for now — the best currently available.

title: Introducing Meerkat: an experiment in global consensus
summary: Cloudflare Research is building a global consensus service called Meerkat that uses a new consensus algorithm called QuePaxa. We plan to use Meerkat to build a strongly consistent, fault-tolerant key-value store, and other applications.

title: Cloudflare proudly joins the UK government's Cyber Resilience Pledge
summary: The pledge is a voluntary framework inviting organizations to commit to foundational cyber security governance, board-level accountability, and supply chain rigor. For over a decade, Cloudflare has pioneered the core pillars of this framework: democratizing security, leadership accountability, and radical transparency.

title: Tame Dependabot: Group your updates, slow the cadence, keep security fast
summary: How one Microsoft project cut Dependabot noise: bundle all updates into a single monthly pull request, while security fixes still land immediately.
details: Dependabot's grouping feature can bundle every dependency update into one pull request per ecosystem instead of firing off a separate PR for each package.
Slowing the update schedule from daily to monthly doesn't weaken security: Dependabot still opens security-fix pull requests immediately, on their own schedule.
A new three-day cooldown delays routine version bumps by default, giving the community time to catch a bad release before it reaches your dependencies.

title: Post-quantum authentication to origins is now supported
summary: Cloudflare now supports post-quantum ML-DSA signatures on the TLS connection it makes to customer origin servers, adding authentication to a rollout that previously only covered encryption.
details: Post-quantum encryption stops an attacker from harvesting encrypted traffic now to decrypt later with a quantum computer, but it doesn't stop someone from forging a certificate to impersonate a server; that's the gap post-quantum authentication closes.

Because Cloudflare controls both ends of its connection to a customer's origin, it could roll out ML-DSA certificates ahead of the public web, which still needs new standards like Merkle Tree Certificates before it can catch up.

Shipping this required updating a TLS library that had gone unpatched for four years, and one of the backlog of changes broke a small number of customers' certificates in production, an outage the team caught and rolled back the same day.

title: BGP ORIGIN attribute manipulation and its impact on the Internet
summary: Cloudflare found that about 70% of BGP routes have their ORIGIN attribute silently rewritten by transit providers, a routing-preference trick used to attract more paid traffic.
details: The BGP ORIGIN attribute is supposed to record how a route entered the network and, per the RFC, should never be changed by anyone else, but transit providers rewrite it anyway because routes flagged IGP get preferred in path selection.
In Cloudflare's testing, six of the sixteen Tier-1 networks manipulated ORIGIN, and doing so won them noticeably more traffic: 18% more paths on IPv4 and 40% more on IPv6.
Cloudflare's proposed fix is to stop routing decisions from relying on ORIGIN at all, arguing every implementation should just treat all routes as IGP so there's nothing left worth gaming.

title: A broken DNSSEC rollover took down .al. Now 1.1.1.1 tells you when validation is bypassed
summary: When Albania's .al domain broke DNSSEC during a botched key rollover, Cloudflare bypassed validation to keep sites reachable, and for the first time told clients directly that it had done so.
details: DNSSEC validation can fail for an entire top-level domain at once if its operator breaks the chain of trust during a key rollover, as happened to .al on July 3, 2026, following a similar incident with Germany's .de two months earlier.

A Negative Trust Anchor lets a resolver keep serving answers for a broken domain by skipping DNSSEC checks, but until now a response served this way looked identical to a fully validated one, with no way for a client to tell the difference.

Cloudflare co-authored a new DNS Extended Error code, EDE 33, that its 1.1.1.1 resolver now attaches to every response served under a Negative Trust Anchor, so monitoring tools and applications can detect when they're getting an unverified answer.

title: Building Service Topology at Scale: Architecture, Challenges, and Lessons Learned
summary: Netflix explains how it built a real-time map of which services call which, and the production problems (Kafka lag, overloaded instances, GC storms) it had to solve to make it work at scale.
details: Raw network logs only show hops through load balancers and proxies, not real application-to-application calls, so Netflix built a three-stage pipeline that regroups and resolves flows by intermediary before writing the final graph.

A single instance handling all traffic for a popular service, like an auth API called by hundreds of others, became a 'hot node' that spent more CPU on garbage collection than on actual work; splitting the pipeline into more redistribution stages spread that load out.

Netflix switched inter-stage communication from gRPC to Server-Sent Events and made aggregator objects mutable instead of immutable on the hot path, both against typical best practice, because measurements showed they cut memory pressure and CPU overhead at their scale.

title: Introducing Precursor: detecting agentic behavior with continuous client-side signals
summary: Cloudflare's new Precursor tool watches behavioral signals like mouse movement and typing rhythm throughout a session, not just at one checkpoint, to tell bots and AI agents apart from humans.
details: Instead of a one-time challenge like a CAPTCHA, Precursor collects behavioral signals continuously throughout a session, so a bot can't just reset its signature by refreshing the page.
It looks for physical constraints that are hard for automation to fake convincingly over a long session, like the natural arc of a wrist movement or the small tremor in a real hand.
The system is built to preserve privacy: it records the timing and rhythm of keystrokes rather than what was actually typed, and it evaluates aggregate patterns instead of individual actions.

title: Disrupting supply chain attacks on npm and GitHub Actions
summary: GitHub breaks down recent changes to npm and GitHub Actions that make supply chain attacks harder to pull off, from safer CI defaults to delayed package publishing.
details: npm now locks high-impact accounts into a 72-hour read-only mode after an email or 2FA-recovery change, closing a window attackers used to hijack accounts.
GitHub Actions changed actions/checkout defaults and added workflow execution policies so fork pull requests can no longer run untrusted code or escalate through shared caches.
npm v12 disables install scripts by default and Dependabot now waits three days before applying non-security updates, cutting the time a compromised package can spread before anyone notices.

title: How Sandstone grew 40x in 147 days on Vercel
summary: Legal-tech startup Sandstone explains how running its whole stack on Vercel, from preview deployments to feature flags, let a small team ship fast enough to grow 40x and raise a $30M Series A.
details: Preview deployments let a non-engineer flag a broken scrollbar and have it fixed in production within five minutes on a Sunday, without a formal deploy process.
Non-engineers can comment directly on preview branches, which automatically turns their feedback into Linear tickets instead of Slack messages that get lost.
Vercel's Secure Compute kept traffic between the app and its data layer off the public internet, avoiding the usual tradeoff of fast iteration for weaker network isolation.

title: Cloudflare Internal DNS is now generally available
summary: Cloudflare's Internal DNS is now generally available, letting companies manage private and public DNS from one platform instead of running separate systems for each.
details: Split-horizon DNS, serving different answers to internal vs external clients, no longer needs two parallel systems; Cloudflare's 'DNS Views' group zones by resolution context instead.
The Gateway Resolver reuses Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 infrastructure to handle recursive resolution and policy checks for private network queries, not just public ones.
DNS changes propagate globally in seconds whether they're made through the dashboard, Terraform, or the API, removing a common source of drift between tools.

title: Content Ingestion & Podcast Video Incident Report
summary: Spotify's postmortem on a podcast video outage: transcoding capacity maxed out, a batch reprocessing job competed for resources, and a migration bug quietly cut throughput by 10%.
details: A routine batch job that reprocessed old episodes ran during peak submission hours, competing with new uploads for the same limited transcoding capacity.
A software bug introduced during an infrastructure migration silently cut processing throughput by about 10%, and it went unnoticed until the capacity crunch made it visible.
Roughly four hours passed between the first alerts and a formal incident response, prompting Spotify to invest in earlier capacity alerting rather than just adding more headroom.
